claims.head: The Jets want Scheifele away from the big guns
claims.call: The Jets’ L1 (Scheifele, Connor and Perfetti) spends at least 38% of its 5-on-5 time against the Hurricanes’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Jets keep sending Scheifele’s line (Scheifele, Connor and Perfetti) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would. That’s Scott Arniel chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Hurricanes’ third line is Staal, Martinook and Ehlers.
claims.nums: At home: 38% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against third lines, about 26% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Scott Arniel likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Hurricanes’ third line.

check.rule: held if the share is at or above the home habit; partly if above the no-matching level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Hurricanes should pile up the shots
claims.call: The Hurricanes take at least their usual 65.8 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: Few teams shoot like the Hurricanes, and the Jets are near the bottom of the league at keeping shots away. It could be a long night in the Jets’ end.
claims.nums: Carolina 3rd for shot volume (65.8 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Winnipeg 24th for shot suppression
claims.gist: The Hurricanes shoot a lot, and the Jets give up plenty.

claims.head: The Hurricanes hound the puck; the Jets sit back
claims.body: The Hurricanes are one of the league’s best for forecheck pressure, at the hounding end; the Jets are one of the league’s worst, at the passive end. Expect that gap to show.
claims.gist: The Hurricanes and the Jets sit at opposite ends for forecheck pressure.
claims.call: The Hurricanes put more forecheck pressure on than the Jets.

notes.text: S. Jarvis has not played this season. He is a top-six forward. W. Carrier has taken his spot beside S. Aho and A. Svechnikov.
L. Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: J. Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 68% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 61 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by N. Ehlers (15 of 18 changes).

notes.text: J. Morrissey is day to day (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-four defenseman. D. Samberg has taken his spot beside D. DeMelo.

WPG.head: Not an easy night for Winnipeg
